page.overview:
What is Pnaklendorf?

Pnaklendorf (also known as The Iron Venus or Uterus Mundi) is a fictional entity created by Ricardo Meyer for his short story "Hain", and is later set to play a major role in "The Machine Beneath Our Feet".

Pnaklendorf is the passive counterpart of the "Unbegotten Source," Ubbo-Sathla, and, like it, remains inactive, immersed in a kind of slumber. It is connected to the earth and occasionally manifests through bodies it materializes, perhaps unconsciously. Although these bodies remain dormant, some retain active vital functions, being capable of giving birth—apparently asexually—to creatures resembling luminous spiders.

What may be its primary body lies within the Dreamlands, and its interior has been colonized, becoming the site where the cities of the so-called "Land of Pnaklendorf" have been built. These colonies, originally devoted to mining, experienced rapid growth due to the abundance of resources. However, over time, the rate of extraction surpassed their capacity for regeneration, leading many inhabitants into precarious conditions. Today, it is a nation marked by deep inequalities, and has served as a place of exile for many of the outcasts of the Dreamlands.

Pnaklendorf is described in two esoteric texts. The oldest is the Liber Veneris, which refers to the "Uterus Mundi," hinting at the existence of a Mother Earth. The second is the Manuscripts of Olleros, an anonymous document transcribed by Professor Hidalgo Pintado of the Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer University and published by Agartha Press in Spain.
